title: Cotype, K-convexity and the approximation property
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) of the cotype-cotype conjecture under the approximation property: a nonzero real Banach space with the approximation property is K-convex if and only if both the space and its dual have finite Rademacher cotype, with possibly different exponents. The core is a decay theorem proved in full: under the approximation property and the two cotype hypotheses, normalized Walsh transforms of vector families decay, and the space contains no uniform copies of the spaces l_1^n. Two classical theorems of Pisier, named hypotheses of the course, connect this to K-convexity. The first lesson gives the definitions, states the theorems, and proves the elementary implications (duality of K-convexity, type and dual cotype, K-convex spaces contain no uniform l_1^n) and the reduction to the decay theorem. The second treats Walsh norms of operators, Kahane's inequality with the constant 24, and moment lifts. The third proves a scalar lemma: an odd bounded function of a sign matrix with prescribed row and column averages has a Fourier coefficient of binary rank at least two. The fourth proves that a slow decrease of Walsh norms forces a large Walsh norm at almost twice the index, through frames and group averaging. The fifth proves uniform decay for finite-rank operators and their norm limits, builds a compact domain with controlled dual moments, proves the decay theorem, and derives a consequence for Grothendieck pairs.
prerequisites: course Foundations of von Neumann algebras, lesson Hahn-Banach, Baire and the basic theorems on Banach spaces: the Hahn-Banach theorem for normed spaces (Corollary 2.3)

course Tensor products of operator algebras, lesson Tensor products of Banach and Hilbert spaces, Jordan homomorphisms and isometries of C*-algebras: the injective and projective norms and their metric mapping property (Proposition 2.4)
finite-dimensional linear algebra over the reals and over F_2; Fourier analysis on finite sign cubes (proved in the third lesson); compactness in finite dimensions
the lessons prove every other fact they use, except the named hypotheses (P) and (MP) of the first lesson and (GMR) and (FTJ) of the last section

open_obligations: Named hypothesis (P): a Banach space that does not contain the spaces l_1^n uniformly is K-convex (Pisier; Pisier's IHP notes, Theorem 4.49). Not proved in the programme; the converse implication of the main theorem and its corollaries depend on it.

Named hypothesis (MP): a Banach space that does not contain the spaces l_1^n uniformly has type p for some p > 1 (Pisier, after Maurey-Pisier; IHP notes, Theorem 4.40(i)). Not proved in the programme; only the forward implication of the main theorem depends on it.

Named hypotheses (GMR) (Gupta-Misra-Ray, arXiv:2305.13270v2, Theorem 1.3) and (FTJ) (Figiel-Tomczak-Jaegermann, in the form of Pisier's ICM 1983 address, Theorem 4): used only for the corollary on Grothendieck pairs.
Missing foundation: a course on type, cotype and K-convexity (Maurey-Pisier theory, Pisier's holomorphic semigroup theorem, Figiel-Tomczak-Jaegermann) would close (P), (MP) and (FTJ).
Not in the course: the entropy-duality consequence of the manuscript's Corollary 1.2, which uses the theorem of Artstein, Milman, Szarek and Tomczak-Jaegermann.
The constants c_*, n_0 and m are existential (compactness in the coefficient lemma); no explicit value is computed.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
